messages:
zoe_cs: Heads-up — onboarding call with LumenHealth uncovered a question about the latency SLO during warmup. They saw token-level latency spikes in the first 30s of each new session and are asking if that counts toward their SLA and whether credits could apply.

mike_reliability: Thanks for flagging. Short answer: transient warmup spikes are expected. Our SLO window is measured per-request average latency over 1m windows, but we don’t want customers to be surprised. We usually exclude background deployment rollouts, but not warm cache behavior unless we’ve agreed in the contract. :thinking_face:

nina_eng: Quick technical note: the spike is due to KV cache population + model init on cold shards. For their workload (many short-lived sessions), the first-turn latency can be 3-4x higher for ~1–2 requests until the prefix cache is populated. We can mitigate with config: sticky sessions or prefetching.

sam_account_mgr: From renewal perspective, LumenHealth is sensitive — they flagged this as a potential risk. They want a customer-facing explanation and a proposed remediation plan before next week’s executive readout. Can we draft a short one-pager and an example of how credits would be calculated if we agreed to carve out warmup windows? :exclamation:

mike_reliability: Proposed comms structure: 1) brief explanation of cause, 2) what we measure (SLO definition + window), 3) recommended config changes (sticky sessions, prefix prefetch), 4) short-term operational options (warmup warmers, preheat on deploy), 5) credit policy proposal with example calculation, 6) next steps & owner.

zoe_cs: Love that. I'll own the customer-facing language. Nina, can you provide one bullet per mitigation with expected latency % improvement and rough implementation ETA? That’ll help show impact rather than just theory.

nina_eng: Sure. Bullets: - sticky sessions (cookie-based routing): ~40–60% reduction in first-turn latency for short sessions; low infra change; ETA 5 business days to enable per-tenant. - prefix prefetch (service-side): ~60–80% improvement but needs limited testing; ETA 2 weeks. - proactive warmup job on deployment: 90% of cases eliminated but costs compute; ETA 3 days to add a one-off job. I’ll attach a short snippet we can use in docs: 

```
# example prewarm curl
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/prewarm -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"gpt-mini","prompts":["init"],"concurrency":2}'
```

sam_account_mgr: Good, include cost tradeoffs in the one-pager. They’ll ask if credits or config changes are cheaper.

zoe_cs: Drafting now. For the credits proposal — suggest we only offer a narrow, example calculation if the customer can show sustained breaches tied to onboarding traffic and cannot adopt preheat within X days. Something like: credit = prorated uptime credit for minutes where average 1m latency > SLO by >30% AND correlate with first-request pattern. Example calc in doc: 

- Contracted SLO: 95th pct tail latency <= 150ms (1m windows)
- Observed warmup minute: average latency 250ms (excess 100ms / 150ms = 0.667) -> translate to credit cap of up to 0.5% for affected minute; then prorate by affected minutes in billing period.

mike_reliability: Prefer to keep the math simple so legal can sign off quickly. Maybe cap credits to a small % of monthly bill (e.g., 2%) and require evidence from our logs. Also add automatic mitigation: if warmup spike pattern repeats after we apply sticky sessions, we escalate to infra.

zoe_cs: Agreed. Nina, please attach the query we'll run to validate warmup-caused breaches. Eg: 

```
-- find sessions with initial-turn latency spike
SELECT session_id, MIN(request_ts) as start_ts, AVG(latency_ms) FILTER (WHERE request_rank=1) as first_turn_latency
FROM request_events
WHERE tenant_id = 'lumen' AND request_ts >= '2026-06-01'
GROUP BY session_id
HAVING AVG(latency_ms) FILTER (WHERE request_rank=1) > 200;
```

nina_eng: I’ll clean that and add correlation flags (cache_miss = true, shard_init = true).

sam_account_mgr: Do we want to offer a free 2-week preheat trial for onboarding? Could be a low-friction remediation that avoids credits and shows good faith.

zoe_cs: Yes — offer trial + the one-pager and a joint follow-up call next Wed. I’ll send to them after we finalize wording. Action items: Zoe (draft + send), Nina (metrics query + mitigation ETA + snippet), Mike (confirm credit cap & legal-friendly phrasing), Sam (customer context and commercial fallback).

uptime-bot: Incident note: No platform-wide SLA incident open. Recent deploys (2026-06-03T08:14Z) included model kernel update to reduce tail variance.

zoe_cs: Thanks. I’ll share draft here by EOD today. If anyone has a hard objection to the 2% credit cap or the trial offer, flag it now so I don’t include it. :eyes: 

mike_reliability: No objection from SRE. 2% cap seems reasonable.

nina_eng: No objections. I’ll drop the refined query into this thread when ready.

sam_account_mgr: All good. I’ll prep the executive context for renewal team.

zoe_cs: Draft posted: https://docs.redwood.ai/short/lumen-warmup-slo-note (internal doc). Please review by 1700. Thanks all. :rocket:
